newsitem.title: UK: Hilton, Ladbroke chiefs to swap board seats.
newsitem.headline: Hilton, Ladbroke chiefs to swap board seats.

text.p: The head of Hilton Hotels of the U.S. and the chief executive of British leisure company Ladbroke Group, owner of Hilton International, will take board seats in each other's companies, newspapers said on Sunday.

The Sunday Telegraph said that Ladbroke's chief executive Peter George and Steve Bollenbach, the head of Hilton Hotels, would publish the plans on Monday as part of a key announcement to unite the Hilton Hotel brand name around the world.
Hilton Hotels owns the rights to the Hilton brand name in the U.S. and Ladbroke owns the rights for the rest of the world.

The two groups, which last August formed an alliance to link up the two groups' reservation and marketing systems for 400 hotels in 49 countries, plan to announce what they have called "their first worldwide initiative" at 1500 GMT in London on Monday, with live video feeds to New York.

Hilton Hotels has already said it plans to take a five percent stake in Ladbroke, which the Sunday Telegraph said would inject about 135 million pounds ($227 million) into Ladbroke if Hilton Hotels buys new shares rather than going into the market.
The Observer newspaper said that Hilton Hotels should increase the five percent stake to a maximun 20 percent holding within three years.
Ladbrokes was not immediately available for comment. ($1=.5950 Pound)
